analysis.headline: Portugal without Ronaldo

pv_hook: Portugal top the group, and tonight they're without Cristiano Ronaldo.
It's Denmark, in Copenhagen. Here's the analysis.
pv_stake: Portugal have won both games and sit top on six points. Denmark and Norway are level on three, fighting for second.
Only the top two go through. A Portugal win would leave Denmark six points behind them.
pv_players: For Denmark, Rasmus Højlund, who scored the only goal the last time Portugal came here, and Mikkel Damsgaard, whose set-pieces made both goals against Wales.
For Portugal, captain Bruno Fernandes, and Gonçalo Ramos, who scored the winner in Oslo.
pv_tactics: Denmark go 4-3-3, with Højlund running the channels and Damsgaard between the lines.
Portugal also go 4-3-3 and like to control midfield. But Norway outshot them 22 shots to 12 in Oslo, and they still won.
pv_model: That is why our model leans Denmark, even with Portugal top: 1.3 expected goals to 1.0.
That's 44% Denmark, 30% the draw, and 26% Portugal.
pv_expect: Expect Portugal on the ball through Bruno and Vitinha, and Denmark to go direct and hunt set-pieces.
The duel to watch is Højlund against Rúben Dias.
Denmark won the last meeting in Copenhagen, 1-0. Our read: tight, with a slight Danish edge at home.
pv_round: Also in this group, Wales host Norway in Cardiff. Wales are still looking for their first point and their first goal.
Erling Haaland has 65 goals in 57 games for Norway. Our model makes Norway favourites, at 56%.
In Group 2, Germany host Serbia in Munich. Klopp is still waiting for his first win as Germany coach.
Serbia have lost both games, and our model has Germany at 79%.
And in Thessaloniki, leaders Greece take on a Dutch side missing four key players.
Our model still makes the Netherlands favourites, at 56%.
pv_cta: That's the analysis. Follow for more football, by the numbers.
